newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Platinum bars vanish on way from S.Africa to Zurich.
newsitem.headline: Platinum bars vanish on way from S.Africa to Zurich.

text.p: Twenty-one bars of South African platinum worth some seven million rand ($1.5 million) have vanished en route to Switzerland, the owner said on Friday.

Police said their diamond and gold unit was investigating the mysterious loss, which apparently occurred somewhere between Johannesburg airport and Zurich, where the precious metal was heading on a South African Airways flight on Tuesday night.

The disappearance of almost half of Anglo American Platinum Corp. Ltd's (Amplats) consignment of bars of refined platinum, which weigh between three and five kg (six and 10 pounds) each, was uncovered by an SAA official in the Swiss banking capital.
"He informed Johannesburg that they had found the seal of the container had been broken and three of the eight holders containing platinum were missing," a police statement said.
An SAA spokesman said the airline was checking who signed for the consignment and whether it had arrived intact at the airport in South Africa's most crime-ridden city.

The missing bars of platinum, whose current market value is $438 an ounce, weigh almost 100 kg (220 lbs) in total. Amplats spokesman Johan Adler said the shipment, which had been taken to the airport by a local security company, was fully insured.
Amplats is the world's biggest platinum producer.
